title: Where’s the party and can you take me there? #Broadway #GreatGatsby #...
transcript: All right, I'll say it. I liked The Great Gatsby musical. Sue Me. And I think that's because in many ways, it feels like a throwback to, like, the mega musicals of the 80s, which we don't really see a lot of nowadays. Like, there's just something about seeing a big Broadway production with lavish sets and costumes and pyrotechnics and big group choreography numbers that is just gonna hit every single time. And that's really what this production of Great Gatsby is like. I fully admit this is not the most intellectual version of The Great Gatsby. This is very much A Great Gatsby that feels designed to run at every regional and high school theater across America. And I think now is a good time to admit that I have actually never read The Great Gatsby. Like, this was kind of my first introduction to the material. And I know that for a lot of people who have read the novel and love the novel, they say that this is not a very faithful adaptation. But for me, with nothing to compare it to and just judging this on its own merits, I think it's a perfectly fine musical. Like, again, it's not Hamilton, it's not gonna change the state of musical theater, but it's enjoyable, and I had a great time. I know that for many people, this is not the version of The Great Gatsby that they wanted, and that is fine and perfectly valid. But For me, I really like what we got. And I, perhaps controversially, don't think that adaptations have to be faithful to the thing that they are adapting. Like, I think people forget The Phantom of the opera is a terrible adaptation of that novel. They took a lot of liberties, and similar to The Great Gatsby, they focused in on the romance aspect, dialed that up to 11, added some spectacle, and said, boom, it's a Broadway musical. And then it became the longest running Broadway show of all time. And obviously, The Great Gatsby as a novel is much more beloved than the Phantom of the opera novel. So obviously, more people are going to come in with expectations of what the story is and should be. But I also think it's important to judge adaptations on their own merits in addition to how they compare to the source material. I'm going to give this Great Gatsby three out of five stars because it's a fun time. It's not a perfect musical. There are certainly things about it that I'm like, yeah, they could have done that a little bit better. But I still had a great time. And if you are someone who likes big, spectacular musicals, I honestly think you're going to have a great time at this show.
